questions.stem: Low insulin: glucagon ratio leads to activation of :
questions.solutionHtml:
Hormone sensitive lipase (hsl)
  • The correct answer is A. Hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL).
  • When insulin levels are low and glucagon levels are high, it indicates a state of low insulin: glucagon ratio.
  • This hormonal imbalance leads to the activation of hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL).


Guyton and Hall textbook of physiology, Edition 14th, page number- 973, Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 326.

questions.stem: In a 35 years old patient, due to intravascular hemolysis, serum K+ increased to 5.5 mEq/L. What will happen to resting membrane potential in this patient :-
questions.solutionHtml:
More positive
  • In the given scenario, with an increased serum K+ concentration of 5.5 mEq/L, the effect on the resting membrane potential would be that it becomes more positive.
  • Elevated extracellular potassium levels can depolarize cell membranes, making the membrane potential less negative or even positive. This depolarization can have various effects on cell function and can lead to alterations in electrical signaling and excitability.
  • Therefore, the correct answer to question is A. More positive.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Physiology, Edition 14th, Page Number: 59-62.

questions.stemHtml: The phases of the ventricular muscle action potential is given below. Which of the following is correctly matched:-

options.label: C
options.text: Transient sodium channel open in phase 3

questions.solutionHtml:
Calcium channel open in phase 2

The characteristic plateau ("2") results from the opening of voltage-sensitive calcium channels.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 491.

questions.stem: Preterm term neonate born at 28 weeks having dyspnoea and b/l lung field . On further investigations ARDS was diagnosed and so is the correct statement for this condition ?

options.label: A
options.text: Surface tension increased and lung compliance decreased

options.label: B
options.text: ST increased and lung compliance increased

options.label: C
options.text: ST decreased and lung compliance decreased

questions.answerText: Surface tension increased and lung compliance decreased
questions.solutionHtml:
Surface tension increased and lung compliance decreased
  • The correct statement for the condition of ARDS (Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome) in a preterm neonate born at 28 weeks with dyspnea and bilateral lung field involvement is:
  • Surface tension increased and lung compliance decreased.


Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.660.

questions.stem: A newborn with respiratory distress syndrome has deficiency of surfactant. Which of the following is seen in this patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase compliance and decreased surface tension

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease compliance and increased surface tension

questions.answerText: Decrease compliance and increased surface tension
questions.solutionHtml:
Decrease compliance and increased surface tension

In a newborn with respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and a deficiency of surfactant, there is a decrease in compliance and an increase in surface tension.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.660.

questions.stemHtml: Regarding the cardiac action potential, which of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Slope of phase 1 is due to opening of sodium channels

options.label: B
options.text: Slope of phase 1 is due to closure of sodium channels

options.label: C
options.text: Slope of phase 3 is due to closure of potassium channels

options.label: D
options.text: Slope of phase 3 is due to closure of calcium channels

questions.answerText: Slope of phase 1 is due to closure of sodium channels
questions.solutionHtml:
Slope of phase 1 is due to closure of sodium channels
  • Phase 1 of the action potential occurs with the inactivation of the fast Na+ channels. The transient net outward current causing the small downward deflection of the action potential is due to the movement of K+ and Cl ions, carried by the Ito and Ito2 currents, respectively.



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 491.

questions.stemHtml: In the adjoining spirogram, which of the following is indicated by the red arrow?
questions.solutionHtml:
ERV
  • Above shown Respiratory volume indicates ERV (expiratory reserve volume ).
  • The ERV is the volume of air that can be forcefully exhaled after a normal resting expiration, leaving only the RV in the lungs. Forcefully exhaling the ERV is an active process requiring the contraction of expiratory muscles in the chest and abdomen.


Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition Page no, 618

questions.stemHtml: Points A to E are given in the adjoining graph of the action potential. Which of the following is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Point A to point C is due to opening of slow sodium channels

options.label: B
options.text: Point C to point D is due to opening of fast potassium channels

options.label: C
options.text: Point E is due to slow closure of sodium channels

options.label: D
options.text: Point B to point D is the refractory period

questions.answerText: Point B to point D is the refractory period
questions.solutionHtml:
Point B to point D is the refractory period
  • The refractory period begins at point B and ends at point D on the action potential curve.
  • This period consists of the absolute refractory period from point B to point C, during which the cell is completely unresponsive, and the relative refractory period from point C to point D, where the cell's responsiveness is gradually recovering but still elevated compared to the resting state.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no 67

questions.stem: A 40 year old male presents with h/o trauma and hemoglobinuria undergoes a series of laboratory investigations. His potassium is 5.5mmol/L. What is the effect on peripheral neurons?

options.label: C
options.text: RMP becomes positive followed by negative

questions.solutionHtml:
RMP becomes less negative
  • The correct answer is B. RMP becomes less negative, as an elevated potassium level reduces the negative charge across the cell membrane, leading to a depolarization of the resting membrane potential. The other options are incorrect based on the effects of increased extracellular potassium levels.
  • The elevated potassium level (5.5 mmol/L) in the presented case can have several effects on peripheral neurons.
  • an elevated potassium level leads to a decrease in the negative charge across the cell membrane, resulting in a depolarization of the RMP.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no 67
